questions.q: What specifically makes governing Microsoft Fabric different from general data governance theory, per this lesson?
options: Fabric has no governance features at all, so none of the theory applies
Every workload shares one tenant-wide lake, so a mistake isn't boxed into one tool — it's visible tenant-wide by default
Fabric only supports a single user per tenant
Governance only matters for the Power BI workload, not the others
questions.explain: Because every Fabric workload stores its data in the same OneLake under one tenant, a permission mistake or ungoverned workspace isn't isolated to one product the way it might be across separate disconnected tools.

questions.q: In one sentence, what is OneLake?
options: A separate storage account you must manually provision for each new workload
The one automatic, tenant-wide data lake that every Fabric workload's data lands in
A third-party cloud storage product unrelated to Fabric
A naming convention for Power BI reports
questions.explain: Every lakehouse, warehouse, and semantic model stores its actual data as folders and files inside OneLake automatically — it's the one underlying lake the whole platform is built on.

questions.q: Which course in this catalog does this lesson say already covers how to build the Fabric items this course teaches you to govern?
options: Data Governance Foundations
Fabric & Real-Time Analytics
Metadata Management & Business Glossary
Power BI
questions.explain: This course assumes you already know how to build a lakehouse, warehouse, or pipeline — that's covered in the separate Fabric & Real-Time Analytics course. This course teaches how to govern what you already know how to build.

questions.q: Per the five-chapter roadmap previewed in this lesson, which chapter covers domains and workspaces?
options: Chapter 1 · Fabric Governance Foundations
Chapter 2 · OneLake
Chapter 4 · Discovery and Lineage
Chapter 5 · Governed Analytics
questions.explain: Chapter 1, Fabric Governance Foundations, covers the tenant, capacity, the admin portal, domains, and workspaces — the structural containers everything else lives inside.

questions.q: According to this lesson, how does ownership of Fabric governance decisions typically shift as an organization scales?
options: It never shifts — one person owns every setting forever
Tenant and capacity settings usually sit with a small central admin team, while domain, workspace, and item-level decisions get distributed to business-unit and workspace owners
All governance decisions are made automatically by Fabric with no human involvement
Only Microsoft support can change any governance setting
questions.explain: Broad, high-blast-radius decisions (tenant/capacity) stay centralized with a small admin team, while narrower decisions get delegated outward to people closer to the data — the same broad-to-narrow order this course follows.
